desc:
Broken link and redirect fixes send every visitor to a real page instead of an error. Ecom Swift LLC scans your store for dead links, repairs each one or redirects it to the closest useful page, and proves the result with a final scan.

## What is a broken link, and why does it hurt a store?

A broken link is a link that leads to a page that no longer exists, usually returning a "page not found" error. It can sit in your menu, a product description, a blog post, an email or an old ad. Each time a shopper clicks it, they hit a dead end and many simply leave.

Search engines notice too. When pages they have indexed start returning errors, they keep trying for a while and then drop those pages. If another site links to a page you deleted, that link value is wasted.

## Where broken links come from

Most stores create them without noticing. A product is deleted after it sells out. A collection is renamed and its address changes. A blog post is moved. A migration from another platform leaves old addresses behind. A staff member types a link by hand and misses a character. Apps and themes can also add links that stop working when a service changes.

Over time these pile up quietly. Nobody sees them, because the store owner rarely clicks old links.

## How fixing links affects traffic and sales

A redirect tells browsers and search engines that a page has moved and where to find it. When it points to a close match, the visitor lands on something useful, such as a similar product or the parent collection. That keeps the visit alive instead of ending it on an error.

For paid traffic, the effect is direct. An ad that points to a dead address pays for a click that can never convert. For organic traffic, clean addresses help search engines keep your pages in their index and pass value from older links. No fix can promise a specific ranking, but removing errors removes an obvious obstacle.

## What a thorough link fix includes

- A crawl of the store's pages, following links as a visitor would.
- Checks of the main menu, footer, breadcrumbs and search results.
- Links inside product descriptions, blog posts and policy pages.
- Links to outside sites, such as suppliers, social profiles and guides.
- Redirects for deleted products and collections that point to the best match.
- Removal of redirect chains, where one redirect leads to another.
- Detection of redirect loops that never resolve.
- A custom not-found page with search and helpful links.
- Review of error pages reported in Google Search Console.
- A final crawl that confirms the fixes.

## What we do

We crawl the store and sort what we find by how visible each problem is. A broken link in the main menu matters more than one in a five-year-old post, so we fix the visible ones first.

For each broken link we choose between three actions. If the target exists under a new address, we correct the link. If the page was deleted and a close match exists, we add a redirect to that match. If neither applies, we remove the link or point it somewhere sensible. You receive a list showing every problem, where it was found and what we did about it. Basic covers a smaller crawl and the most visible fixes. Standard widens the crawl, handles redirects for removed items and checks outside links. Premium adds redirect clean-up, the error page and Search Console errors.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Redirect a deleted product to a similar product or its collection.
- Set up a redirect whenever you rename a page address.
- Keep a simple record of every redirect you create.
- Check links again after any large import or migration.
- Make your error page helpful, with search and popular links.

**Avoid:**
- Sending every dead address to the home page, which confuses visitors.
- Stacking redirects so that one leads to another.
- Deleting pages without checking what links to them.
- Pasting links into emails and ads without testing them.
- Ignoring link problems because the store looks fine from your own device.

## Who this is for

This suits a store that has recently changed platforms or themes and fears old addresses were lost. It suits a seller with a long-running catalog where products come and go. It also suits anyone who runs ads or email campaigns and wants every click to land on a working page.

## What we need from you

Send us your store address, any known problem pages and the platform you use. For Search Console work, add us as a user on your property. We work as a collaborator, staff or admin user in your own account, and we never need your password.
